title: Building an Inclusive Team Culture 🧑‍🤝‍🧑
description: Shift left, train teams, hire inclusively, and establish accessibility champions and governance.

slides.title: Accessibility Is Everyone's Job 🧑‍💻
slides.content:
From designers to developers, testers, product managers, and executives – everyone owns a piece of accessibility.

- **Designers**: choose colours, typography, and interaction patterns.
- **Developers**: write semantic HTML, manage focus, add ARIA.
- **Testers**: run automated and manual audits.
- **PMs**: prioritize a11y in the backlog, define acceptance criteria.
- **Leadership**: fund training, set policy, measure progress.

Accessibility can't be one person's side hustle – it must be woven into the fabric of the team.

quizData.question: Who should be responsible for accessibility in a product team?

options.text: Every team member, from design to QA

quizData.explanation: Accessibility is a shared responsibility across roles.

slides.title: Training & Upskilling 📚
slides.content:
Invest in continuous learning:

- **Awareness workshops** – 1‑2 hour intro for all staff.
- **Role‑specific training** – deep dives for designers (contrast, focus), developers (semantic HTML, ARIA).
- **Certification** – IAAP CPACC, WAS, or similar.
- **Lunch & learns**, internal knowledge sharing.

Set a baseline: every developer should know how to test with a screen reader. Every designer should know WCAG contrast ratios.

quizData.question: What is the IAAP CPACC certification?

options.text: Certified Professional in Accessibility Core Competencies

quizData.explanation: CPACC is a globally recognized accessibility professional credential.

slides.title: Shifting Left: Embedding Accessibility Early 🏗️
slides.content:
Accessibility shouldn't be a last‑minute audit. Integrate it throughout the development lifecycle:

- **Design reviews**: contrast checks, focus order, annotate accessibility.
- **Code reviews**: include a11y checklist, use linters.
- **CI/CD**: run automated tests on every PR.
- **Definition of Done**: include a11y acceptance criteria.

The earlier you catch an issue, the cheaper it is to fix.

quizData.question: What does 'shift left' mean in accessibility?

options.text: Testing earlier in the development cycle (design, code review, CI)

quizData.explanation: Shift left means catching accessibility issues as early as possible.

slides.title: Inclusive Hiring & Employee Experience 🤝
slides.content:
Accessibility isn't just for external users. Your own tools and processes must be accessible.

- Use accessible HR platforms and job boards.
- Offer reasonable accommodations in interviews.
- Provide accessible internal tools, documents, and communication.
- Ensure remote work setups are accessible.

Hiring people with disabilities brings firsthand insight into accessibility gaps.

slides.title: Accessibility Champions & Governance 🛡️
slides.content:
Establish a network of accessibility champions across teams. Appoint a central a11y lead or team to:

- Define standards and best practices.
- Provide training and support.
- Review critical features.
- Advocate at the leadership level.

Without governance, accessibility efforts fizzle out.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## Celebrate accessibility wins
Recognize teams that fix critical bugs or ship accessible features. Positive reinforcement drives culture change.
